title: Cedar Foundations
subtitle: Permit, forbid, and the request shape
content:
✅ Permit, ⛔ Forbid, 🤷 Default Deny

Cedar decides Allow iff at least one permit matches AND no forbid matches. Everything else denies. Three canonical policies below are quoted from the Cedar documentation set (verified Sept 2026):

Cedar: specific permit, conditional permit, overriding forbid 
// Last verified: 2026-09 vs cedar-policy/cedar-docs syntax-policy.md
permit (
    principal == User::"alice",
    action == Action::"view",
    resource == Photo::"VacationPhoto94.jpg"
);

// Owner-scoped edit: when-condition binds resource to principal
permit (
    principal,
    action == Action::"editPhoto",
    resource
)
when {
    resource.owner == principal
};

// Forbid wins: private photos stay private (permit alone is not enough)
forbid (
    principal,
    action,
    resource
)
when {
    resource.private
}
unless {
    principal == resource.owner
};
// Last verified: 2026-09 vs cedar-policy/cedar-docs syntax-policy.md permit ( principal == User::"alice", action == Action::"view", resource == Photo::"VacationPhoto94.jpg" ); // Owner-scoped edit: when-condition binds resource to principal permit ( principal, action == Action::"editPhoto", resource ) when { resource.owner == principal }; // Forbid wins: private photos stay private (permit alone is not enough) forbid ( principal, action, resource ) when { resource.private } unless { principal == resource.owner };

📨 The Authorization Request (Terminology, Verified)

Cedar docs define an authorization request as principal × action × resource × context: the app supplies entity details (principals, resources), context (IP, auth method, time), and the policy set; the engine returns decision + determining policies. If you remember the XACML boxes from Lesson 3, this is the same idea with Cedar nouns.

Cedar request: entities + context travel with every call 
// SHAPE-ILLUSTRATIVE entity/request JSON — the exact 'cedar authorize'
// flags and __entity/type+id forms vary by CLI version. Confirm with
// 'cedar authorize --help' for your pinned version before scripting.
// Semantics (principal/action/resource/context + entity attrs) verified
// 2026-09 vs cedar-policy/cedar-docs terminology.
// Entities the app must supply:
{ "uid": { "type": "User", "id": "alice" },
  "attrs": { "department": "finance", "clearance": 3 },
  "parents": [{ "type": "Team", "id": "eng" }] }

// Request: alice views VacationPhoto94.jpg from office IP with MFA
{ "principal": "User::\"alice\"", "action": "Action::\"view\"",
  "resource": "Photo::\"VacationPhoto94.jpg\"",
  "context": { "ip": "10.0.4.12", "mfa": true } }
// SHAPE-ILLUSTRATIVE entity/request JSON — the exact 'cedar authorize' // flags and __entity/type+id forms vary by CLI version. Confirm with // 'cedar authorize --help' for your pinned version before scripting. // Semantics (principal/action/resource/context + entity attrs) verified // 2026-09 vs cedar-policy/cedar-docs terminology. // Entities the app must supply: { "uid": { "type": "User", "id": "alice" }, "attrs": { "department": "finance", "clearance": 3 }, "parents": [{ "type": "Team", "id": "eng" }] } // Request: alice views VacationPhoto94.jpg from office IP with MFA { "principal": "User::\"alice\"", "action": "Action::\"view\"", "resource": "Photo::\"VacationPhoto94.jpg\"", "context": { "ip": "10.0.4.12", "mfa": true } }

🔍 Critical Review Notes

  • Forbid is not standalone: the docs are explicit — a forbid-only set denies everything because no permit matches. Every forbid needs its permit partner.
  • unless vs when: when must hold for the policy to apply; unless must NOT hold. The private-photo forbid reads: applies when private, except when requester is owner.
  • Rego vs Cedar instinct check: Rego asks is allow derivable?; Cedar asks does a permit match AND no forbid match? Both default-deny; Cedar makes the override explicit.
🎮 Try it in the Policy Lab → Run the four photo scenarios: public vs private × owner vs stranger. Use the controls under the canvas to switch scenarios and watch the verdict change.

questions.question: When does Cedar return Allow?

options.text: At least one permit matches AND no forbid matches
When no policy matches at all
When a forbid matches, regardless of permits
Only when every permit in the set matches

questions.explanation: Cedar's own terminology: decision Allow requires a matching permit and zero matching forbids. Forbid always overrides.

questions.question: Bob views Alice's private photo. A permit matches (public-view rule) and the private-photo forbid matches. Verdict?

options.text: Deny — forbid overrides permit
Allow — permit was listed first
Allow — Bob asked politely
Error — policies conflict

questions.explanation: Order is irrelevant in Cedar; forbid wins by semantics, not position. The unless-owner escape is what saves Alice viewing her own private photo.

questions.question: In forbid(...) when { resource.private } unless { principal == resource.owner }, what does unless do?

options.text: The forbid does NOT apply when the requester is the owner
The forbid applies ONLY to the owner
It is a comment with no effect
It converts the forbid into a permit

questions.explanation: unless = negative condition. Policy applies when when-holds AND unless-does-not-hold. Owner viewing own private photo escapes the forbid.

questions.question: A Cedar request must include which four elements?

options.text: Principal, action, resource, context (+ entities and policies)
Username and password only
IP address only
The full database

questions.explanation: Per Cedar terminology: the engine evaluates (principal, action, resource, context) against entities + policies and returns decision + determining policies.

questions.question: A policy set contains ONLY forbid policies. What happens to all requests?

options.text: All deny — no permit can match
All allow — forbids are ignored alone
The engine crashes
Only admins are affected

questions.explanation: Docs-verified: forbid only restricts; granting requires a permit. Forbid-only sets are a classic misconfiguration this quiz exists to prevent.

questions.question: An isAuthorized call omits context.mfa but policy branches on it. Result?

options.text: Attribute access errors — the erroring policy is skipped, deny follows; check errors diagnostics and the schema
The engine defaults it to true
The engine guesses from the IP
Automatic permit for resilience

questions.explanation: Missing-attribute access is an evaluation error, not false: skip-on-error plus default-deny yields deny. Debug via errors diagnostics, prevent via schema validation.

questions.question: Restate forbid(...) when {A} unless {B} as prose.

options.text: Forbids when A holds, except where B holds
Forbids only when A and B both hold
Permits when A holds
Ignores B entirely

questions.explanation: when gates applicability; unless carves the exception. Misreading the polarity inverts the protection.

questions.question: Two permits match overlapping scopes. Result?

options.text: Allow — one matching permit suffices; forbids are still checked
Deny — overlapping permits are ambiguous
Engine error on overlap
First-listed permit wins, rest ignored

questions.explanation: Permits are existential, not exclusive. Order never matters in Cedar — only match plus absence of forbid.
